newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony says considering headquarter functions in US.
newsitem.headline: Sony says considering headquarter functions in US.

text.p: Sony Corp chairman Norio Oga told reporters on Thursday that the company is seriously considering adding "second headquarter" functions to its U.S. unit, Sony Corp of America.

"It is getting very difficult to control everything from Japan, and we could miss the bus now that American sales account for 30 percent of the group (sales), more than Japan's 20 percent," Oga told a news conference.
Sony Corp of America now controls Sony's entertainment business in America, but will be given more strategic functions as a second headquarters, Oga said.
Asked about the planned listing of Sony's U.S. film unit, Sony Pictures Entertainment, Sony president Nobuyuki Idei said the listing was "just one future business option".
Idei also said Sony will set up a consumer electronic marketing company, Sony Marketing (Japan) Inc, on April 1.
The new company will have eight sales units under its wing, and 1997/98 sales are projected at 480 billion yen, Sony said.
Sony will also set up a new group to handle digital satellite broadcast-related business.
It will control business such as content, television set-top boxes and base stations, which are currently handled by several different Sony units.
Although Sony is optimistic about its business this calendar year, Oga said he was "very concerned about the severe business conditions" in Japan.
